title: Free a jammed steering lock: turn the wheel off the bolt and hold it there while the key turns to ON
context: A car with a keyed ignition was parked and its steering wheel was moved after the key came out. The column lock's bolt dropped into its collar, and the wind-up stored in the front tyres now presses the collar's notch onto the bolt, so the key's cam cannot draw it back and the key will not turn. Most drivers of keyed cars meet this. The fix is two-handed and is not just holding a sprung part still while a key turns: the wheel must first be turned off the bolt the one way it gives (the other way is a dead stop, so the robot has to find it), then held inside the collar's few degrees of play while the tyres try to spin it back, and the key turned while still holding. Forcing the key alone does nothing and can snap it.
setup: Positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y to the left) in cm; heights are above the table. A driver's-end steering column, fixed to the table, raked 25 degrees from horizontal and rising towards the robot, which sits in the driver's place. Steering wheel: NVIDIA SimReady steeringSystem_steering_wheel_e01, 35.0 x 32.8 cm, black rim of 3 x 4 cm section, spokes at 3, 6 and 9 o'clock, 1.0 kg; centre at (25, 0), 22 cm up, face to the robot; it turns on the column's axis, plus or minus 25 degrees. Column shroud: black ABS, 19.5 cm long, 10 cm wide, 12 cm tall, from 13.5 cm behind the rim's mid-plane, entering the dash. Inside it: an 18 mm steel shaft with a steel lock collar (44 mm across, one notch 6 mm deep, 8 degrees of play past the bolt) and the lock's steel bolt (8 x 10 x 25 mm, 8 mm travel), engaged. Ignition on the shroud's right: black ABS housing 52 mm across, its axis parallel to the column 12 cm right of and 4.5 cm below its axis, face centre at (39, -12), 10.5 cm up, with a chrome bezel and marks clockwise as the driver sees them: white LOCK 0, amber ACC 30, green ON 65, red START 88 degrees. Key: nickel-silver blade, black plastic head 32 x 26 x 11 mm (head centre at (37.3, -12), 11.3 cm up), 30 g, at LOCK. Start state: the wheel pressed clockwise onto the bolt with 8 N m (a torsion spring standing in for the tyres: 0.5 N m per degree, at rest 16 degrees past the notch's wall). Dash: black boards, a 2 x 50 x 30 cm face at x 50 to 52 and a 22 x 50 cm ledge on top (x 50 to 72), 30 cm up. Distractors (SimReady, loose): sunglasses (accessory_eyeglasses_a01, 14.5 x 17.4 x 5.7 cm, 30 g) on the ledge at (61, 14), turned 90 degrees; a paper coffee cup with lid (food_beverage_coffeeCup_a01, 8.5 cm across, 11.7 cm tall, 250 g) at (58, 36); the car's service book (misc_notebook_a01, 22.9 x 17 x 1 cm, 120 g) at (33, 39), turned 17 degrees. Both grippers start open at their ready poses.
scoring: Read from the key's angle (real trial: a photo of the key's head against the bezel marks) and the grippers' distance from the key's head (video). 1.0: the key rests in its ON detent (60 to 70 degrees) with every fingertip point of both grippers (each finger's tip and 3 cm up it) at least 3 cm from the key's head, held 2 s; scored 1.0 from then on. 0.5: at the end, the key rests in ACC (25 to 40 degrees) with both grippers 3 cm clear of its head. 0: anything else, including the key at ON but held by a gripper. Any trial in which the key was forced before full credit scores 0: more than 2.45 N m through the key for 0.15 s (simulation; real trial: a bent or snapped key, or the wrist's torque log). The wheel is not scored: a hand may still hold it at the end, at any angle. A turn to START is allowed: it springs back to ON.
reset_notes: Turn the key back to LOCK, turn the wheel until the bolt drops into the collar's notch, then turn the wheel clockwise onto the bolt and load it to 8 N m (52 N on a luggage scale hooked on the rim at 9 o'clock, 15.5 cm from the axis) and let go.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (PhysX, 240 Hz). The tyres' wind-up is a spring on the wheel's joint; its 8 N m and 0.5 N m/degree are estimates, not measurements. The bolt is pinched by contact friction (0.65) and its guide's friction; the key-to-bolt cam is code (a stiff coupling each step, pull capped at 120 N). Key detents are springs. Wheel travel is cut at 25 degrees. The wheel is SimReady with hull colliders; column, lock and dash are primitives.
